figureObjective: Compare ideal series and parallel resistor circuits using matched positive resistors and the same battery voltage.

claims.text: Series components are connected one after another in the same branch and carry the same current.
Parallel resistors share the same two nodes and therefore have the same voltage drop.
Parallel branch currents may differ, but they split and recombine so their sum equals the battery current.
Series resistance sums directly; parallel conductances sum and the parallel equivalent is less than the smallest positive branch resistance.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 19.2, paragraphs fs-id1167064901800 and fs-id1167065821410; official PDF pages 637-638
anchors.normalizedText: Series components are connected one after another in one branch, with the same current through the original circuit and its equivalent resistor.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 19.3, paragraphs fs-id1167065746966 and fs-id1167065978239; official PDF page 641
anchors.normalizedText: Parallel resistors have both ends connected directly together, so the voltage drop across each resistor is the same.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 19.3, paragraphs fs-id1167062315741 and fs-id1167065843479; official PDF pages 641-642
anchors.normalizedEquation: I = I1 + I2 + I3; branch currents need not be equal

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 19.2 equation 19.13 and 19.3 equation 19.28; paragraphs fs-id1167066197380 and fs-id1167065761913; official PDF pages 639 and 642
OpenStax Physics 19.3, paragraph fs-id1167065722817; official PDF page 641
anchors.exactQuote: Therefore, the equivalent resistance must be less than the smallest resistance of the parallel resistors.

elements.meaning: One ideal branch containing positive resistors R1, R2, and R3.
Three ideal branches sharing the same two nodes.
Conventional current I supplied by the common ideal battery.
Currents I1, I2, and I3 that split and recombine in the parallel circuit.
The two nodes common to both ends of every parallel resistor.

allowedVariation.rule: Circuits may be horizontal or vertical if connectivity and distinct parallel nodes remain unambiguous.
IEC or ANSI resistor glyphs may be used consistently without changing connectivity.
Battery enclosure and background may vary; wires, junctions, arrows, and labels remain evidentiary.

mutations.description: Show different steady-state currents through series elements without a branch or transient condition.
Use Req(parallel) = R1 + R2 + R3 or claim the parallel equivalent exceeds the largest branch resistance.
Omit or misplace a junction so intended parallel branches become series-connected or disconnected.
Draw branch-current arrows that split but do not recombine while retaining steady-state conservation.
